positions.stance: Says civil liberties are non-negotiable; opposes banning any social media app and mandates prohibiting peaceful assembly.
Opposes wasteful government spending, with a focus on ending corporate welfare.
Says people should stop asking government permission on hot-button issues like abortion and charter schools and instead find solutions through public conversation.
Says representatives should publicly notify constituents when lobbyists approach them and return unused office money to the U.S. Treasury.
Supports term limits, suggesting U.S. Representatives be limited to about four terms.

wiki:chad-humphrey.name: Chad Humphrey
wiki:chad-humphrey.bio: Retired Marine Corps officer (1993-2013) and tech entrepreneur.

positions.stance: "Restore the Constitution."
"End the Fed and the IRS."
"Stop the Endless wars."
Names free markets as the policy area he is personally passionate about.

H0CO03173.name: Critter Milton
H0CO03173.bio: Former financial advisor of over a decade who lives in Alma, Colorado.

positions.stance: Favors term limits, saying an ongoing transition of power at all levels of government would be healthy for the system.

wiki:johnny-baucom.name: Johnny Baucom
wiki:johnny-baucom.bio: National Guard veteran who has managed multiple mechanic shops.

positions.stance: Will not approve anything at taxpayer expense: no budget expansions without cuts elsewhere and no raises for Congress.
Would work on deregulation, starting with ending the EU Deforestation Regulation's hold on U.S. lumber so the industry can set its own standard.
Says laws punishing crimes with no victims need to be repealed.
Says defending your life and property with a firearm of your choice is an inherent American right.
Says the freedom of unfiltered, even unpopular, speech "never shall it be infringed."

H6MS03236.name: Erik Kiehle
H6MS03236.bio: Property management businessman, volunteer firefighter for two Lauderdale County departments, and private pilot.

positions.stance: Will vote against spending bills that add to the federal debt and push for a constitutional amendment requiring balanced budgets.
"End the foreign wars by ending all spending for the Ukraine and Iran wars."
"End all aid to Israel."
"Mass Deportations and ban all Muslim immigrants."
Says the nation cannot spend its way to affordability and that current spending puts children into more debt.
Calls for ending the wars, saying "Both sides fund Isreal and fund genocide."
Says any solution to the nation's financial problems must be bipartisan, since both parties created them.

az-sos-2026-fontes-adrian.name: Adrian Fontes
az-sos-2026-fontes-adrian.bio: Arizona Secretary of State, elected in 2022; former Maricopa County Recorder, prosecutor, and U.S. Marine Corps veteran.

positions.stance: Will protect Arizona's established voting methods, including early voting, vote-by-mail and in-person voting, which he says have multiple layers of security.
Will protect the privacy of Arizona voters' data from unauthorized disclosure, including federal requests beyond what Arizona law permits.
Will increase transparency and voter education and advocate for county resources and more state and federal funding to modernize and secure election systems.
Will continue to fight misinformation and seek sustained investment in voter registration systems, ballot tracking and administrative tools.

md-ag-2026-brown-anthony.name: Anthony G. Brown
md-ag-2026-brown-anthony.bio: Maryland Attorney General; former Lieutenant Governor, member of Congress, state legislator and U.S. Army veteran.

positions.stance: The office's federal actions team works to protect civil and voting rights, education and health care access, immigrant communities and LGBTQIA+ rights.
Works with the Public Defender and university researchers to reduce racial disparities in Maryland's criminal justice system and recommend policy changes.
Works to protect Marylanders from hate crimes and discrimination through a state commission, a reporting portal, and community and police partnerships.
Leads Maryland's legal response to the Key Bridge collapse, seeking to recover costs so Maryland taxpayers don't pay them.
Administers a commission researching historical racially motivated lynchings in Maryland and holding public meetings in affected communities.

source.label: their Maryland Attorney General office website
